name: Angel Reaper

tenures.source: The Georgia region's own In Memory of the Fallen supercard broadcast of 31 May 1998
tenures.note: Retained the CWC Southern States Championship in a scaffold match against Ian Walker on 31 May 1998; both men fell from the scaffold locked in a piledriver attempt, and Reaper was ruled the winner for landing on top in the safety net below.

caption: Retained the CWC Southern States Championship in a scaffold match against Ian Walker after both men fell together, ruled the winner for landing on top in the safety net.

identity.note: An existing museum character shares this exact name (a member of the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse, New York City/WWA titles). No shared operator, roster, or promotion is read this pass to connect the two beyond the bare ring name; 'Angel Reaper' is a common enough gimmick name to have arisen independently.

name: Ian Walker

tenures.source: The Georgia region's own In Memory of the Fallen supercard broadcast of 31 May 1998
tenures.note: Sprayed mace into John Weyrauch's eyes to help his own Supreme Fighting Empire stablemates win the Georgia State Tag Team Championship, then challenged unsuccessfully for the Southern States Championship in the scaffold match main event.

caption: Challenged for the CWC Southern States Championship in a scaffold match, coming closer than the result showed before both men fell into the safety net together.

name: Warren Worthington III
caption: A British aristocrat gimmick who withdrew from the Georgia Cup tag tournament rather than team with an American partner, then was forced back into action at Heat Wave '98 when Commissioner Bob Lane threatened to void his contract.
